html:
A short agreement signed by 41 men aboard the ship Mayflower in November 1620, before they landed to found Plymouth Colony in what is now Massachusetts. It was the colony's first governing document.

The passengers were a mix: Separatist Puritans, later called the Pilgrims, who had left the Church of England, and others who came for work or land. Their charter was for land in Virginia, but the ship arrived far north of it, and some threatened to do as they pleased once ashore. The compact bound everyone to form a "civil body politic" and obey the "just and equal laws" it would make for the general good, while still declaring loyalty to King James.

It was not a constitution, but it rested government on the consent of the settlers themselves. Later Americans saw it as an early step toward self rule, part of the story that led to the Declaration of Independence. The Pilgrims were followed a decade later by the larger Puritan migration.
